hypothesis: If the claim holds, then among living mammals with paired cranial weapons, only deer have a weapon that is solid throughout, and only deer cast that weapon.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered (both clauses). Solid-throughout means the headgear character table codes the keratin sheath as absent. Casting means the table codes regeneration of bone tissue as present. Sheath-only replacement is not casting: Aristotle's other animals keep the bony core, and he says deer cast the solid horn. The solid-only clause passes if cervids are solid-throughout and no other coded family is. The shed-only clause passes if cervids regenerate bone and no other coded family does. Both clauses must pass. Cell codes: '+' present, '-' absent, '(+)' present, '(-)' absent, '+/-' means the state occurs in some members of the family. A '+/-' outside cervids on the deer-like state (sheath absent, or bone regenerated) makes that only-clause fail. A '?' leaves that family unscored; a definite counterexample in another family still fails the clause.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Verdict 'supports' only if both only-clauses pass. Verdict 'mixed' if exactly one only-clause passes and the other fails. Verdict 'refutes' if both only-clauses fail. Verdict 'inconclusive' with reason 'underpowered' if a clause is unscored because of '?' and there is no definite counterexample, and the other clause does not independently fail. Verdict 'inconclusive' with reason 'data-unavailable' if Table 1 cannot be fetched or the two character rows cannot be identified. Rhinocerotidae is added only if the same article's prose states whether a rhinoceros horn is a hollow sheath over a bony core or a solid mass, and whether it is shed; otherwise rhinos are not invented into the table. Confidence: 0.70 if all four ruminant families have definite codes on both characters; 0.50 if any used cell is '?'; 0.35 if inconclusive.
interpretation: Horns here are the cranial weapons Aristotle is contrasting with deer: he says other horns are hollow for a distance, with a bony core set into the cavity, whereas deer horns are solid throughout and are cast. That is the bovid sheath-over-core against the cervid antler of bone. Solid-throughout is therefore absence of a keratin sheath, not a density measurement. Casting is shedding and replacing the bone, not shedding a keratin sheath from a permanent core. Giraffe ossicones and pronghorns are inside the comparison because they are headgear of horned mammals, which is the claim's scope. The test does not ask whether every individual deer has antlers.

test_contract.expected_observation: In the four-family headgear table, only the cervid column lacks a keratin sheath and only the cervid column regenerates the bone.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Another family lacks a keratin sheath, or another family regenerates the bony weapon, or cervids themselves have a sheath or do not regenerate bone.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: A published comparative table of living ruminant headgear that scores sheath and bone regeneration separately for cervids, bovids, giraffids and antilocaprids, from dissection and natural-history observation rather than from Aristotle.
test_contract.inference_method: Transcribe Table 1's keratin-sheath and bone-regeneration cells and apply the only-clause rules and the verdict table in the criteria. No average across families.

caveats: A web-search snippet had already displayed an HTML rendering of this table before the commit. The snippet is not the measurement. The script must read the article and transcribe the cells.
The table does not include rhinoceroses unless the article text does. A pass would then be a pass inside ruminant headgear, which the caveat must repeat if that is the outcome.

Analysis: Giraffe ossicones are scored solid-throughout because Table 1 codes their epidermis as having no keratin sheath. Pronghorns regenerate the keratin sheath and not the bone, so they are not scored as casting the horn.
Analysis: Rhinoceroses are outside this table. The article page contains no rhinoceros wording, so they were not coded.

datasets.name: Davis, Brakora and Lee 2011, Table 1, Evolution of ruminant headgear
datasets.license: Full text publicly readable on PMC; copyright The Royal Society 2011
datasets.role: character table of keratin sheath and bone regeneration for cervids, bovids, giraffids and antilocaprids

measured.unit: only-clauses that hold (solid-throughout exclusive to deer; bone-casting exclusive to deer)

method: Fetched the PMC HTML of Table 1 and the article, transcribed the keratin-sheath row and the regeneration-of-bone-tissue row for the four families, and applied the pre-registered only-clause rules. A keratin sheath absent is solid-throughout; regeneration of bone is casting. Sheath-only renewal is not casting. The article HTML does not mention rhinoceroses, so Rhinocerotidae was not added.
results_summary: Keratin sheath codes: cervids=-, bovids=+, giraffids=-, antilocaprids=+.
Bone regeneration codes: cervids=+, bovids=-, giraffids=-, antilocaprids=-.
Solid-only clause fail; shed-only clause pass. giraffids lack a keratin sheath (solid bone under skin) and do not regenerate it.
